I used to make up stories and tell them to her at bedtime, but now she interrupts and makes up her own stories instead. However, I notice that her own small desires are embedded within them. Later, as she encounters more media, she'll learn how to express these desires with more sophisticated grammar. The important thing is to imagine and create. I don't place any restrictions on this. My daughter always kills Germ King (the villain from Cocomong). (In the actual animation, there are no death scenes.) I wonder how a child who can't even watch a chase scene comes up with stories where villains are brutally killed. I try to suggest that Germ King was just led astray by bad friends, but it seems children prefer simplicity, and the desire to punish what is scary and bad is still strong in them. These examples alone show that children's violence isn't caused by media violence, but rather by defense mechanisms or relational issues. My son is violent, or more accurately, animalistic (a human beagle), but I don't think this is due to media influence. Dinosaurs constantly eating each other... all I've shown him is Octonauts. He can't even watch realistic dinosaur documentaries because he finds them scary. ㅡoㅡ
I'm also learning through my children. Honestly, I don't know if there's a right answer. A characteristic of software is learning through failure. I believe teaching children is the same. What's certain is that they love doing things and talking with their dad.
I'll do the same when they watch webtoons later.
You might ask, "How can you do that when you're so busy? Shouldn't society protect them from all harmful things?"

{{IMG:4}}
                                
                            Are children really that important? So you're just going to leave them to society and neglect them?

To break your prejudice about webtoons, I'll recommend one that's even more uncomfortable for parents to read than "Bastard."

**Danji** Thirty-one, 10 months since moving out. Thinking back, I... have never experienced what others consider a family, not even for a moment. titleEn: I'm More Worried About Parents Who Don't Understand Their Bratty Kids.
contentEn:
I saw a post on my timeline about the webtoon 'Bastard,' rated for all ages, expressing concern that children might watch it. I also raise a child, but because I remember encountering a lot of media and arguing with my parents when I was young, my feeling upon seeing this post was '꼰대' (old-fashioned/boomer).

[**평범한 아빠의 네이버 고소 이유? 웹툰의 전체이용가 진실 – Daum 아고라** m.bbs3.agora.media.daum.net](http://m.bbs3.agora.media.daum.net/gaia/do/mobile/petition/read?bbsId=P001&objCate1=1&articleId=187769&pageIndex=1)

The gist of it is that, based solely on the overall plot and expressions, it's harmful and shouldn't be watched. They mentioned having elementary and middle school children. I also raise a child. If I were to show this webtoon to Saebom, she would probably find it boring at first. There's too much text for children below elementary school age to read. And they might say it's too stimulating and scary. However, big and small stimuli are everywhere. When reading children's books, the range of expression is the issue; there are stories that deal with the death of parents, and children say they are sad.

[**후레자식** '내 집안에 살인마가 산다.' 본격 세대갈등 잔혹 스릴러 comic.naver.com](http://comic.naver.com/webtoon/list.nhn?titleId=628997)

This is not because children don't know about murder or killing, but because it's not within their scope of understanding. The moment it enters their scope of understanding, it can be scary or confusing. **No child will see the title 'Bastard' and think, 'Oh, I should try murdering too.' If they do, you've raised them poorly. You've turned your child into a robot.** It's like thinking that if they play games, they'll go outside and start shooting guns. On the contrary, the more you block external stimuli, the less they can tolerate even small stimuli, or they exhibit overreactions. This phenomenon also occurs with chocolate or games. I wonder if they read the 'Bastard' webtoon from beginning to end. **Demanding an R-rating based only on a captured image from the text is like demanding an R-rating for a wrestling screenshot because it looks suggestive (and it's even a homosexual work!).** **It's about the confrontation with a murderer father and twisted love-hate, not about the child being a bastard because the father is a murderer. I can't give you the detailed plot as it might be a spoiler, but please read it once.** If you want to stop your child, first watch/read it thoroughly yourself. It's a webtoon that offers a lot to think about. **I believe that media which provides food for thought, like this, can be more educational than spoon-fed educational materials. In my case, I actually developed my thinking skills through such media rather than textbooks.** **At the very least, play the game and read the webtoon before making a judgment.** **And, the first thing to do is not to sue, but to have a conversation with your child. Find out what your child felt and learned. If there's a problem with that, then it might truly be an issue with the work itself. (However, don't use leading questions.)** **If you did that without doing this, you've acted 100% like a '꼰대'. You've lost 10 points of trust with your children.**

{{IMG:1}}
TIG One Sound, 'How to Identify a Gamer Child'

Actually, of course, there are webtoons I would want to stop children from seeing. In these cases, it's not professional webtoons, but rather indiscriminate webtoons produced and distributed among children themselves, which sometimes cross the line by only depicting desires. The same goes for games ([http://goo.gl/oBrpPo](http://goo.gl/oBrpPo))

http://www.thisisgame.com/webzine/series/nboard/213/?series=42&page=3&n=47975
[**[TIG Cartoon] How to Identify a Gamer Child** [Warning] This video contains brutal scenes from <The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim>. www.thisisgame.com](http://www.thisisgame.com/webzine/series/nboard/213/?series=42&page=3&n=47975)

At least, the stimuli from webtoons and various media that are processed and provided to us are rarely as harmful as one might think. While it's partly true that we might become desensitized to stimuli, is our society one without stimuli? If I turn on the news, it's often too terrible to watch. Is it as terrible as a society where children speak disrespectfully to their deceased parents? Let's not cover our children's eyes. It's even more regrettable that the plaintiff is an ordinary father. Since when have our fathers become so isolated from their children?

{{IMG:2}}
Princess Mononoke

I will see the world with eyes unclouded.

From Princess Mononoke. Unlike Studio Ghibli's usual style, heads fly off and people die in droves, yet it's rated for all ages. What our children need is not just to have their eyes covered. Consider whether you are raising your child like a hothouse flower. **Becoming a '꼰대' is not a matter of age; it's a matter of empathy. Let them decide on media for themselves.**

I was worried because it was cloudy and rainy during the week two weeks ago, but it was sunny on the weekend. In fact, even the fine dust cleared, making it perfect for going out with the kids. The place we arrived at had this kind of view. The modern building in the upper right is Onar Pool Villa.

1. Pool Villa Overview

{{IMG:27}}
                                
                            Onar Pool Villa distant view

Looking a bit closer... it's a truly modern detached house. You see two doors, right? The leftmost one is the pool connected to the villa, and the middle door is the entrance.

{{IMG:28}}
                                
                            Onar Pool Villa private house

But we arrived a bit early. They were still filling the pool. ㅜㅜ Fortunately, there was also a wonderful outdoor pool, so our kids immediately took to it. My son and daughter were eager to get in. My heart pounded when they went close without life jackets. After strongly urging them to be careful, I hurriedly pulled out their life jackets from our luggage and put them on.

2. Outdoor Pool

{{IMG:29}}
                                
                            Onar Outdoor Pool, Kids eager to enter

Looking from a bit further away, the pool looks like this.

{{IMG:30}}
                                
                            Onar Outdoor Pool, distant view

The water depth was about waist-high. There were two parasols, outdoor chairs, and even large tubes provided, so you could actually just show up and play.

{{IMG:31}}
                                
                            Onar Pension, Outdoor Pool, Parasols

The luggage under that parasol is ours. They put our luggage in the refrigerator of another building right next door, so we could also enjoy cool fruits.

{{IMG:32}}
                                
                            Beach Tube

The tube was so large that I could ride it with my child. If you tell the owner about the tubes you brought, he'll inflate them with a compressor. Even large boats can be inflated quickly. My second child, Ikyeom, was initially afraid of the water because he remembered falling into the sea last year while playing with his mom, but after riding on his mom's belly, he later asked to play more.

{{IMG:33}}
                                
                            Ikyeom (second child) overjoyed on mom's belly

There are many more photos with excited expressions, but I'm reluctant to reveal my children's faces these days, so I won't share them.

{{IMG:34}}
                                
                            Panorama Photo

3. Indoor Pool Villa with Spa

After playing outside, the pool was fully filled, so we came inside the pool villa. When we entered, we saw this view~! We could use this spacious pool all to ourselves. Haha.

{{IMG:35}}
                                
                            Onar Pension Private Indoor Pool

{{IMG:36}}
                                
                            Onar Pension, Spa

What you see above the pool is a spa. Actually, when you just swim, your body can get a bit cold, so you can fill the spa with water, warm up, and then go back into the pool. It's large enough for about 3 adults. There's an air conditioner, but since it wasn't the peak of summer, we didn't turn it on. Next to the pool, there's also a table and chairs, allowing for dining, and it connects directly to the barbecue area. It seemed like you could grill meat in the barbecue area and eat it right there at the table and chairs. However, we grilled the meat in the barbecue area and brought it inside to eat, so we didn't use that particular spot.

{{IMG:37}}
                                
                            Onar Pension Private Indoor Pool 2

And the reason we didn't really need to use that dining table was that if you open the sliding door right next to the pool, it connects directly to the interior of the pension.

4. Sunbeds and Lounge

When you open the sliding door, two sunbeds are beautifully placed. From the sunbeds, you can see the beautiful sky and watch the children playing in the pool.

{{IMG:38}}
                                
                            Sky viewed from the sunbed

{{IMG:39}}
                                
                            Pool viewed from the pension

And to the right, there's a space like a lounge. It looked like a charming spot to have some tea. If you look at the kitchen photo later, there's also a coffee maker.

{{IMG:40}}
                                
                            Lounge with a pretty painting

5. Master Bedroom

Next to the reception room is the master bedroom, the largest room. There are a total of 2 rooms. In addition to the bathroom in the living room, each room also has its own bathroom, making a total of 3 bathrooms. Naturally, all of them include shower booths. The pool villa has a standard capacity and can accommodate up to 6 people. In other words, it can accommodate up to 3 couples. You might be wondering how it works with only two rooms? I'll explain that later.

{{IMG:41}}
                                
                            Master bedroom next to the central living room

{{IMG:42}}
                                
                            Two large beds.

A large master bedroom that seems big enough for a large family, with two large beds. Our family came with my mother-in-law, and we stayed in this room, while my mother-in-law stayed in the adjacent room.

{{IMG:43}}
                                
                            And a TV and dressing table

You can also access the pool from the master bedroom. The door visible next to it leads directly to the pool.

6. Small Room

When I got home, I realized I hadn't taken any photos of the small room where my mother-in-law stayed. ㅜㅜ It also has a large bed of similar size, a big LCD TV, and a spacious bathroom/shower booth attached. While not as large as the master bedroom, it's as clean and spacious as a large room in a typical two-person pension.

7. Living Room

The living room has a generously sized sofa... it was wider and more comfortable than our sofa at home. We were at that table.

{{IMG:44}}
                                
                            Onar Pool Villa Living Room

Ta-da... This is why we travel, isn't it?

{{IMG:45}}

Our kids rolled around on the soft carpet, so I was careful, as it seemed like it might be difficult to clean... Fortunately, a vacuum cleaner was provided, so I vacuumed the carpet before we left. Earlier, I mentioned 3 couples, and you might have found it strange that there are only 2 rooms, right? The secret lies in these stairs next to the bathroom.

{{IMG:46}}
                                
                            Loft stairs

Climbing those stairs reveals a beautiful loft space. It's designed so that the top isn't easily visible from below, which seems to protect privacy, and there's also a small table. While you can't stand upright, it's a sufficient space when sitting, and it doesn't feel particularly low.

{{IMG:47}}

8. Kitchen

The kitchen is important for good eating. First, the kitchen shelves are stocked with coffee mats and various convenience items.

{{IMG:48}}

A spacious double-door refrigerator, water purifier, toaster, and a full set of microwave oven!

{{IMG:49}}

Plenty of cups of various sizes on the shelf,

{{IMG:50}}

The faucet is generous, and there's a 2-burner induction cooktop.

{{IMG:51}}
                                
                            Dining table

My wife said she wished she had a kitchen like this ㅜㅜ How many pyeong would an apartment need to have a kitchen like this?

{{IMG:52}}
                                
                            Kitchen overview

9. Charming Entrance

Next to the kitchen is this beautiful entrance. Instead of going straight outside, there's a turn and a middle door.

{{IMG:53}}
                                
                            Entrance

10. BBQ

When you think of a pension, you think of BBQ. I diligently grilled and carried the food inside. The kids had been playing in the water, so I couldn't eat outside in case they got cold.

{{IMG:54}}
                                
                            BBQ area

The view from the BBQ area is also wide open.

{{IMG:55}}
                                
                            View from the BBQ area

11. And a Charming Night View

Perhaps because it's summer, the days have gotten longer. A panoramic view of the pool villa pension taken from outside. It looks very peaceful.

{{IMG:56}}

And, the evening view of the reception room.

{{IMG:57}}

And there's a piano too! ^^ Since it's a private villa, you can play it to your heart's content. My wife, who loves it, says the acoustic piano feels much better than our digital one at home. (Even though our digital piano at home wasn't cheap... ㅜㅜ The acoustic feel is just different.)

{{IMG:58}}

I enjoyed the relaxed feeling that you can't experience in an apartment. It was a good break, eating well and having fun. Even if it feels a bit expensive, the reason to go to a pool villa seems to be for that sense of relaxation. While there's a certain charm to visiting crowded places in the summer, when you're jostled by people, you can't tell if you went to relax or to suffer. Moreover, if you have young children, there are countless things to worry about. The distance isn't too far, so it might be good to come and relax. I wonder if I'll ever be able to live in a house like this when I get older?

12. Modern and Special Other Spa Pensions and Glamping Units

In addition to the pool villa, there are also other modern and wonderful spa pensions and glamping units that offer a camping atmosphere. They also offer pickup service, so please refer to the link below.
